Recent research supports separating recommendation relevance, explanation quality, and factual support. [ALERT (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.naacl-long.137/) evaluates explanations across Amazon categories and reports 70% concordance with expert judgments—useful, but insufficient to treat automated judgments as ground truth. [Human Feedback Is Not Gold Standard (2024)](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/f719b8ca81221f380836e573d479c223-Abstract-Conference.html) shows that assertiveness can distort factuality judgments. Persuasive explanations and positive preference ratings therefore require separate evidence checks.

For the twenty-user audit, a practical synthesis is to record item identity, exact feedback, supporting title/description passages, and judgment status separately. Explicit rejection supports a negative judgment within its stated scope; “choose now” indicates contextual preference, not permanent usefulness; missing identity makes item-specific assessment unresolvable. Assess specificity through concrete supported attributes, redundancy through documented overlap, and prerequisites only when explicitly stated. Text similarity can flag possible duplication but cannot establish usefulness, ownership, compatibility, or satisfaction. Keep simulator traits unknown; distinguish simulated feedback from human observations. These are proposed audit rules, not validated findings from these papers.

Abstention needs calibration: [AbstentionBench (2025)](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/fb122bfc3f0127a94ded048b5b03496f-Abstract-Datasets_and_Benchmarks_Track.html) finds persistent failures on underspecified and unanswerable questions. Use supported/contradicted/unknown labels with evidence spans; manually review ambiguous cases and a sample of confident judgments. Report evidence coverage, unsupported-claim rate, abstention rate, and human agreement alongside relevance and redundancy. Treat this small audit as exploratory diagnosis; retain the pinned macro validation HR@10 for model selection.
